points: The next earnings print could reveal Q3 2026 organic growth slowing, after reported Q1/Q2 commercial P&C premium declines, and any cut to Q4 guidance would confirm the short thesis.

The FTC’s ongoing review of AJG’s AssuredPartners acquisition could produce a material remedy or fine before year-end; the DOJ already settled with AssuredPartners for $135 million, so the >$100 million fine falsifier is a realistic downside trigger.

AI-native insurance tools, including OpenAI’s offerings, could gain customer adoption through Q4 2026 and into 2027, compressing brokerage commissions; even compression well below the 10% falsifier level would squeeze AJG’s high-fixed-cost model.
Peers GSHD and RYAN report on Oct 22 and Oct 30, likely before AJG, and if they flag weaker pricing or AI-driven commission pressure, AJG’s valuation could re-rate lower ahead of its own print.

AJG holds 10.3% of the $95 billion U.S. commercial brokerage commission market, leaving it heavily exposed to any continued premium decline; if Q3/Q4 premiums keep falling at the Q2 pace, revenue growth could turn negative in 2027.

The Sept 30 retirement of the Controller/CAO and Oct 1 appointment of a replacement add near-term accounting and integration risk, especially while the AssuredPartners deal remains under regulatory review.

Recent acquisitions, including Apollo Insurance Solutions, may not deliver expected synergies if integration costs rise; the falsifier is a >15% cost overrun, but even smaller overruns plus falling premiums would pressure margins in H1 2027.
